title: SPaCeD: Spatial Point Process Distances for Pairing the Heavy and Light Chains of B Cell Receptors from Spatial BCR-seq
abstract: We introduce SPaCeD, a framework that infers B cell receptor (BCR) heavy light chain pairs from spatial BCR-seq by integrating expression matrices with spatial point process distances. In ovarian and breast cancer datasets and simulations, SPaCeD improves pairing recall and stability compared with existing methodology (Repair), particularly for pairs with lower spatial expression. More broadly, SPaCeD provides a framework for representing spatial omics data as spatial statistical objects.

title: A transcriptomic-driven segmentation and cell simulation framework for high-resolution spatial transcriptomics and cell-cell communication
abstract: High-resolution spatial transcriptomics platforms, such as Visium HD and Atera, enable transcriptome-wide profiling at near-single-cell resolution. However, accurate cell segmentation to define spatial boundaries relies heavily on histological images. Previous approaches struggle in tissues with high cell density, inflammation, or mineralization, leading to transcriptomic bleed-through and inaccurate clustering. To address this, we developed TENGU (Transcript-signal Enrichment and Grouping Unit), a comprehensive end-to-end bioinformatic software package. Unlike existing tools, TENGU employs a transcript-first segmentation approach, prioritizing transcript-signal density as the primary modality and utilizing histological images only as a secondary supplement in unresolved regions. These initial boundaries are further optimized through a transcriptomic-driven cell simulation algorithm that iteratively refines boundaries based on localized gene expression probabilities, effectively minimizing spatial scattering and preserving biologically distinct molecular signatures. The pipeline seamlessly integrates tissue segmentation, high-resolution cell-type annotation, and spatially aware cell-cell communication (CCC) analysis. We rigorously benchmarked TENGU against the 10x Genomics and Bin2cell pipelines for segmentation, and against CellNEST for spatial CCC inference, across diverse and technically challenging microenvironments. TENGU demonstrated superior transcriptomic distinctness in the murine brain and successfully captured matrix-embedded osteocytes in decalcified bone. In murine osteomyelitis, TENGU outperformed CellNEST in sensitivity, localizing both reactive bone remodeling (Tgfb) and dense, abscess-encapsulating inflammatory (Il1a/Il1) networks. TENGU also resolved species-specific pro-tumorigenic hubs (MDK-SDC4) in a human colorectal cancer xenograft and generalized effectively to the Atera platform, delineating CXCL12-CXCR4 and LGALS3-TGFBR2 signaling within highly compacted human breast cancer tissue. By mitigating image-dependent constraints, TENGU provides a highly adaptable, robust computational framework to decode the functional micro-anatomy of healthy and pathological tissues.

title: Organ context dominates cell identity across a multi-organ single-cell atlas of grapevine
abstract: How transcriptional programs defining cell identity are maintained or remodeled across organ contexts remains a fundamental question in plant biology, particularly in long-lived perennials. We generated a multi-organ single-nucleus transcriptomic atlas of the dwarf grapevine cultivar Pixie, comprising over 220,000 nuclei from nine organs across vegetative and reproductive development, each sampled in two biological replicates. We annotated 46 distinct cell types and anatomical structures, reconstructed developmental trajectories within selected cell types, and inferred gene regulatory networks at cell-type resolution. Organ identity accounted for 65% of regulon activity variance across the atlas compared to only 17% for cell type, demonstrating that organ context is the dominant driver of transcriptional variation in most shared cell types. Broadly distributed cell types including epidermis and xylem parenchyma underwent extensive organ-specific reprogramming, while companion cells maintained organ-independent regulatory programs across all nine organs, representing the stable end of a continuum of transcriptional plasticity. This finding suggests that companion cell identity is buffered against organ context, consistent with their invariant role in phloem loading. This atlas establishes a reference framework for dissecting gene regulatory network organization across organs in a perennial crop and provides a resource for cell-type-resolved functional genomics in grapevine and other woody perennials.
